title: IoT, Cloud, E-Commerce & ICT – Subject Test

questions.q: Google App Engine, which lets developers deploy their code without managing servers or operating systems, is best classified as:
questions.exp: It provides a platform (runtime and tools) for building applications, which is Platform as a Service.

questions.q: Which statement about RTGS in India is correct?
options: It settles high-value payments in real time on a gross basis
It settles payments in half-hourly batches on a net basis
It is used only for payments below ₹1000
It works only for card payments
questions.exp: RTGS = Real Time Gross Settlement, meant for large-value transfers.

questions.q: What is the hexadecimal equivalent of the decimal number 255?
questions.exp: 255 = 15 × 16 + 15, which is FF; hexadecimal 100 equals 256.

questions.q: Which of the following is an open-source cloud computing platform used to build IaaS clouds?
questions.exp: OpenStack is an open-source IaaS platform.

questions.q: Which of the following is the fastest storage location in a computer system?
questions.exp: Registers sit inside the CPU and have the lowest access time in the memory hierarchy.

questions.q: In MS Excel, cells A1, A2 and A3 contain 4, 6 and 5 respectively. What is the value of =SUM(A1:A3)*2?
The Unified Payments Interface (UPI) in India was developed by:
questions.exp: UPI was developed by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI).

questions.q: Which of the following is an international standard for Electronic Data Interchange?
questions.exp: UN/EDIFACT (and ANSI X12 in the USA) are EDI message standards.

questions.q: Which sensor is commonly used to measure the intensity of ambient light?
questions.exp: An LDR changes its resistance with incident light; the others sense temperature, magnetic field and pressure/vibration.

questions.q: In MS Excel, which shortcut inserts the current system date in the active cell?
questions.exp: Ctrl+; inserts the date, Ctrl+Shift+; inserts the time and Ctrl+D fills down.

questions.q: A processor has a 16-bit address bus. What is the maximum memory it can directly address?
questions.exp: 2^16 = 65536 locations = 64 KB (for byte-addressable memory).

questions.q: A cloud infrastructure shared by several organizations that have common concerns such as security requirements and compliance policies is called a:
questions.exp: Community cloud serves a specific community of organizations with shared concerns.

questions.q: Which key combination switches between the open windows in Microsoft Windows?
questions.exp: Alt+Tab cycles windows; Win+D shows the desktop and Alt+F4 closes the active window.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the three original Vs of Big Data?
questions.exp: The original 3 Vs are Volume, Velocity and Variety; vulnerability is not a V of big data.

questions.q: The Digital India programme was launched by the Government of India in the year:
questions.exp: Digital India was launched on 1 July 2015.

questions.q: Which of the following is the largest unit of data storage?
questions.exp: Order: GB < TB < PB < EB.

questions.q:
Statement I: MQTT runs over TCP.
Statement II: CoAP uses UDP and supports multicast.
Which option is correct?
options: Statement I is true and Statement II is false
Statement I is false and Statement II is true
questions.exp: MQTT is TCP-based; CoAP is UDP-based and supports multicast and resource discovery.

questions.q: Who developed the Linux kernel in 1991?
questions.exp: Linus Torvalds created the Linux kernel.

questions.q: Which statement about Ethereum smart contracts is correct?
options: They are self-executing programs stored and run on the blockchain
They are paper agreements digitally scanned
They can be altered by one administrator at any time
questions.exp: A smart contract's code executes automatically when conditions are met and is stored on-chain.

questions.q: Who is credited with writing the first algorithm meant to be executed on a machine, for Babbage's Analytical Engine?
questions.exp: Ada Lovelace's notes on the Analytical Engine contained an algorithm to compute Bernoulli numbers, regarded as the first program.

questions.q: Which frequency is used by High Frequency (HF) RFID and NFC systems?
questions.exp: HF RFID and NFC operate at 13.56 MHz.

questions.q: A freelance designer offers logo-design services to companies through an online marketplace. This model is:
questions.exp: An individual offering a service to businesses is consumer-to-business.

questions.q: A program that replicates itself by attaching to other executable files and spreads when the infected file is run is a:
questions.exp: A virus needs a host file; a worm spreads independently.

questions.q: Which Indian law mainly deals with cybercrime and electronic commerce?
questions.exp: The IT Act, 2000 provides legal recognition to e-records and defines cyber offences.

questions.q: Duty cycling in battery-powered wireless sensor nodes is mainly used to:
options: Save energy by periodically putting the radio to sleep
Select the shortest route to the sink
questions.exp: The radio is the major energy consumer, so nodes sleep for most of the time.

questions.q: Who invented the World Wide Web in 1989-91 while working at CERN?
questions.exp: Tim Berners-Lee proposed the WWW, HTML and HTTP at CERN.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Digital signatures provide non-repudiation.
Reason (R): A digital signature is created with the signer's private key, which only the signer possesses.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is false but Reason is true
questions.exp: Because only the signer holds the private key, the signer cannot deny having signed, so R explains A.

questions.q: MongoDB is an example of which type of NoSQL database?
questions.exp: MongoDB stores data as JSON-like (BSON) documents.

questions.q: Issuing of birth certificates online to citizens is an example of which type of e-governance interaction?
questions.exp: Government delivering services to citizens is G2C.

questions.q: What makes the blocks in a blockchain linked together and the chain tamper-evident?
options: Each block stores the IP address of its miner
Each block stores the private key of the sender
Each block stores the hash of the previous block
Each block stores a timestamp of the next block
questions.exp: Changing any block alters its hash and breaks the previous-hash link stored in the next block.

questions.q: Which of the following helps reduce power consumption in a data centre?
options: Running every server at idle continuously
Installing more standalone physical servers for each application
questions.exp: Virtualization lets fewer physical servers run many workloads, saving power.

questions.q: Which network topology is NOT supported by ZigBee?
questions.exp: ZigBee supports star, mesh and cluster-tree topologies only.

questions.q: Which of the following is a Type 2 (hosted) hypervisor?
questions.exp: VirtualBox runs on top of a host operating system.

questions.q: Which of the following is a classic example of a C2C e-commerce platform?
questions.exp: OLX is an online classifieds site where consumers sell to other consumers.

questions.q: Which statement about compilers is correct?
options: A compiler executes the source program line by line without producing object code
A compiler converts machine code into source code
A compiler translates the whole source program into machine code before execution
A compiler manages the files of the OS
questions.exp: Interpreters work line by line; compilers translate the complete program.

questions.q: Which of the following is an absolute cell reference in MS Excel?
questions.exp: An absolute reference fixes both column and row with $ signs; B$2 and $B2 are mixed.

questions.q: Convert 3 MB into KB, taking 1 MB = 1024 KB.
questions.exp: 3 × 1024 = 3072 KB; 3145728 is the number of bytes.

questions.q: Which of the following was the first general-purpose electronic digital computer, completed in 1946?
questions.exp: ENIAC (1946) was the first large general-purpose electronic computer; Mark I was electromechanical and EDSAC (1949) was stored-program.

questions.q: Which of the following is a professional networking website?
questions.exp: LinkedIn is designed for professional networking and recruitment.

questions.q: A bank keeps its customer data in its own private cloud but uses a public cloud for handling peak web traffic. This deployment is a:
questions.exp: Combining private and public clouds is a hybrid cloud.

questions.q:
Match the instruments with the quantity they measure:
1. Anemometer  2. Hygrometer  3. Barometer
(a) Humidity  (b) Atmospheric pressure  (c) Wind speed
questions.exp: Anemometer measures wind speed, hygrometer humidity and barometer atmospheric pressure.

questions.q: Which generation of mobile networks first introduced digital voice transmission (GSM) and SMS text messaging?
questions.exp: 1G was analog; 2G made voice digital and introduced SMS.

questions.q: UMANG, the mobile app for government services, stands for:
options: Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance
Universal Mobile App for National Government
United Mobile Access for New Governance
Unique Mobile Application for National Growth
questions.exp: UMANG provides many central and state e-services on a single platform.

questions.q: In MQTT, which Quality of Service (QoS) level guarantees that a message is delivered exactly once?
questions.exp: QoS 0 is at most once, QoS 1 at least once and QoS 2 exactly once; there is no QoS 3.

questions.q: Which MS Excel function counts only the cells that contain numbers in a range?
questions.exp: COUNT counts numeric cells; COUNTA counts all non-empty cells.

questions.q: The Android operating system is based on which kernel?
questions.exp: Android is built on the Linux kernel.

questions.q: The JAM trinity, used for direct benefit transfer in India, stands for:
questions.exp: JAM links Jan Dhan bank accounts, Aadhaar identity and mobile numbers.

questions.q: Which technology allows two devices to exchange data when brought within a few centimetres of each other, as used in contactless payments?
questions.exp: Near Field Communication works at about 4 cm at 13.56 MHz.

questions.q: VoLTE stands for:
questions.exp: VoLTE carries voice calls as data over 4G LTE networks.

questions.q: Which cloud service model gives the consumer control over the operating system, storage and deployed applications, but not over the underlying physical infrastructure?
questions.exp: With IaaS the consumer rents virtual machines and manages the OS and above.

questions.q: NB-IoT (Narrowband IoT) operates in:
questions.exp: NB-IoT is a 3GPP LPWAN technology deployed in licensed cellular bands.

questions.q: In mobile telephony, SIM stands for:
questions.exp: A SIM card stores the subscriber's identity and authentication keys.

questions.q: An ENERGY STAR label on a computer or monitor indicates that the product:
options: Is made entirely of recycled plastic
Is free of all software licences
questions.exp: ENERGY STAR certifies energy-efficient products.

questions.q: In MS Word, which shortcut key opens the Find and Replace dialog box with the Replace tab active?
questions.exp: Ctrl+H opens Replace; Ctrl+F opens Find/Navigation, Ctrl+R right-aligns and Ctrl+P prints.

questions.q: Which statement about passive RFID tags is correct?
options: They carry an internal battery that lets them transmit for kilometres
They work only when connected to a Wi-Fi router
They have no battery and are powered by the reader's radio-frequency field
They require a SIM card to transmit
questions.exp: Passive tags harvest energy from the reader's RF signal to respond.

questions.q: Which of the following is an output device?
questions.exp: A plotter produces hard-copy drawings; the others are input devices.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of semi-structured data?
questions.exp: JSON and XML carry tags/keys but no fixed relational schema, so they are semi-structured.

questions.q: In MS Word, which shortcut centre-aligns the selected paragraph?
questions.exp: Ctrl+E centres, Ctrl+J justifies, Ctrl+L left-aligns and Ctrl+R right-aligns.

questions.q: In a cellular network, the process of transferring an ongoing call from one base station to another is called:
questions.exp: Handoff (handover) maintains a call as the user moves between cells.

questions.q:
Statement I: A digital footprint is the trail of data left by a user's online activities.
Statement II: Phishing is a malware attack that encrypts a victim's files and demands ransom.
Which option is correct?
options: Statement I is true and Statement II is false
Statement I is false and Statement II is true
questions.exp: Statement I is true. Statement II describes ransomware; phishing is a deceptive attempt to steal credentials.

questions.q: By default, CoAP (Constrained Application Protocol) runs over which transport protocol?
questions.exp: CoAP is a lightweight REST-like protocol designed for constrained devices and uses UDP.

questions.q: In MS PowerPoint, which key starts the slide show from the first slide?
questions.exp: F5 starts from the beginning; Shift+F5 starts from the current slide.

questions.q: ZigBee is based on which IEEE standard for low-rate wireless personal area networks?
questions.exp: ZigBee builds its network and application layers on the IEEE 802.15.4 PHY and MAC.

questions.q: The BharatNet project primarily aims to:
options: Provide high-speed broadband connectivity to gram panchayats using optical fibre
questions.exp: BharatNet connects rural gram panchayats under Digital India.

questions.q: What is the default TCP port used by an MQTT broker for unencrypted connections?
questions.exp: MQTT uses port 1883 for plain connections; 8883 is used for MQTT over TLS, and 5683 is the CoAP UDP port.

questions.q: Apache Spark is generally faster than classic Hadoop MapReduce mainly because it:
options: Performs in-memory processing of intermediate data
Compresses all output into one file
questions.exp: Spark keeps intermediate results in memory instead of writing to disk after each step.

questions.q: ZigBee devices operating in the 2.4 GHz band offer a maximum data rate of about:
questions.exp: IEEE 802.15.4 at 2.4 GHz gives 250 kbps.

questions.q: The padlock symbol and 'https' in a browser's address bar indicate that:
options: The website is owned by the government
Data between browser and server is encrypted using TLS/SSL
The computer is free of viruses
questions.exp: HTTPS uses TLS/SSL to encrypt communication.

questions.q: Which essential characteristic of cloud computing means resources can be automatically scaled up and down with demand?
questions.exp: Rapid elasticity lets capacity expand or shrink as demand changes.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of a public blockchain?
options: Controlled by a single central authority
questions.exp: Public blockchains have no single controlling authority.

questions.q: How many bits are there in 2 KB, taking 1 KB = 1024 bytes?
A tyre manufacturer sells directly through its web portal to car-making companies. Which e-commerce model does this represent?
questions.exp: Business selling to another business is B2B.

questions.q: Which consensus mechanism is used by the Bitcoin network?
questions.exp: Bitcoin miners compete to solve a hash puzzle, which is Proof of Work.

questions.q: Which of the following is a Low-Power Wide-Area Network (LPWAN) technology commonly used in IoT?
questions.exp: LoRaWAN offers long range at low power and data rate.

questions.q: What is the sum of the binary numbers 1011 and 0110?
'Cloud bursting' refers to:
options: Deleting all data from a cloud
A sudden failure of all data centres
Temporarily using public cloud resources when private cloud capacity is exhausted
questions.exp: It is a hybrid cloud technique for handling demand spikes.

questions.q: Which essential cloud characteristic allows the provider to meter usage and bill customers on a pay-as-you-go basis?
questions.exp: Measured service means usage is monitored and billed accordingly.

questions.q: The SHA-256 hash function produces a hash value of:
questions.exp: SHA-256 gives a 256-bit digest, used in Bitcoin.

questions.q: In IoT, edge computing refers to:
options: Storing all data permanently in a remote data centre
Connecting devices only through satellite links
Processing data close to where it is generated instead of sending everything to a central cloud
Encrypting data using only symmetric keys
questions.exp: Edge computing reduces latency and bandwidth use by local processing.

questions.q: An Aadhaar number issued by UIDAI consists of how many digits?
questions.exp: Aadhaar is a 12-digit unique identification number.

questions.q: In Hadoop's HDFS architecture, which node stores the file-system metadata (namespace and block locations)?
questions.exp: The NameNode keeps metadata while DataNodes store the actual blocks.

questions.q:
Match the inventor with the invention:
1. Blaise Pascal  2. Charles Babbage  3. Herman Hollerith  4. John Napier
(a) Pascaline  (b) Difference Engine  (c) Punched-card tabulating machine  (d) Logarithms and Napier's bones
questions.exp: Pascal built the Pascaline, Babbage the Difference Engine, Hollerith the tabulator and Napier invented logarithms and Napier's bones.

questions.q: The very first block of a blockchain is known as the:
questions.exp: The first block, which has no previous block, is called the genesis block.

questions.q: Which Government of India platform allows citizens to store and share digital copies of documents such as driving licence and mark sheets?
questions.exp: DigiLocker is the cloud-based document wallet under Digital India.

questions.q: A Type 1 (bare-metal) hypervisor is one that:
options: Runs as an ordinary application on top of a host operating system
Runs directly on the host hardware without a host operating system
Is a physical network switch connecting virtual machines
Is available only as a SaaS product
questions.exp: Type 1 hypervisors such as VMware ESXi and Xen run directly on hardware.

questions.q: Compared with barcodes, RFID tags can be read:
options: Only after being scanned by a laser at 1 cm
Without a direct line of sight
questions.exp: Radio waves do not need line-of-sight reading.

questions.q: How many kilobytes are there in 1 GB (taking 1 KB = 1024 bytes)?
Which IEEE standard describes Bluetooth-type wireless personal area networking?
questions.exp: 802.15.1 was the basis of Bluetooth, while 802.15.4 is used by ZigBee.

questions.q: Which of the following is a recommended green computing practice?
options: Enabling sleep or power-saving mode on idle computers
Keeping all desktops switched on overnight for updates
Using animated screen savers instead of sleep mode
Throwing old monitors into ordinary household waste
questions.exp: Power management reduces energy consumption of idle systems.

questions.q: What is the ASCII code (decimal) of the capital letter 'D', given that 'A' is 65?
questions.exp: A=65, B=66, C=67, D=68; 100 is the code of lowercase 'd'.

questions.q: In MS Word, which shortcut inserts a page break?
questions.exp: Ctrl+Enter inserts a page break; Shift+Enter inserts a line break.

questions.q: Which of the following is a SaaS offering?
questions.exp: Google Docs is application software delivered over the web.

questions.q: The BIOS (basic input/output system) program of a PC is stored in:
options: A ROM/flash chip on the motherboard
questions.exp: BIOS is firmware kept in non-volatile ROM/flash memory so it is available at power-on.

questions.q: In the MQTT protocol, the server that receives messages from publishers and forwards them to the subscribed clients is called the:
questions.exp: MQTT follows a publish-subscribe model mediated by a broker.

questions.q: In an IoT system, the main role of a gateway is to:
options: Bridge local device protocols such as ZigBee or BLE to IP networks and the cloud
Replace all sensors in the network
questions.exp: Gateways translate between constrained-device protocols and the internet.

questions.q: Which generation of computers used integrated circuits (ICs) as the main electronic component?
questions.exp: First used vacuum tubes, second transistors, third ICs, fourth microprocessors (VLSI).

questions.q: EDI in e-commerce stands for:
questions.exp: EDI is the computer-to-computer exchange of standardised business documents.

questions.q: Netiquette refers to:
options: Accepted rules of polite and responsible behaviour on the internet
questions.exp: Netiquette is network etiquette for online conduct.

questions.q: In the three-layer architecture of the Internet of Things, which layer is responsible for sensing physical quantities and identifying objects?
questions.exp: The perception (sensing) layer contains sensors, actuators and tags that collect data from the physical world.

questions.q: In a credit card transaction, the 'acquiring bank' is the bank that:
options: Issues the credit card to the customer
Prints the card and sends it to the customer
Regulates all banks in the country
Holds the merchant's account and processes card payments on its behalf
questions.exp: The acquirer serves the merchant; the issuer serves the cardholder.
